title: The etale site of a thickening
statement:
If $T''\to T'$ is a thickening of schemes (a closed immersion
inducing a homeomorphism of the underlying spaces), then the
small etale site of $T''$ is the
same as that of $T'$: pullback along $T''\to T'$ induces an
isomorphism of sites, hence an equivalence of the categories of
etale sheaves identifying the
cohomology of the two schemes.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Proposition 59.45.4,
[Tag `03SI`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SI).*)

proof.text: A thickening is a surjective closed immersion, so the existing lemma on surjective closed immersions gives that its structure morphism is a universal homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04EX, Definition definition-thickening (1); proof of Tag 09ZV, Lemma lemma-thicken-property-morphisms; Tag 04DF, Lemma lemma-universal-homeomorphism

proof.text: For a universal homeomorphism, base change gives an equivalence between the categories of etale schemes, and it preserves and reflects jointly-surjective covering families. Therefore pullback identifies the small etale sites (their objects, morphisms, and covering families).

source.place: Tag 04DZ, Theorem theorem-topological-invariance; Tag 03SI, Proposition proposition-topological-invariance (1)

proof.text: Apply the topological-invariance proposition to the universal homeomorphism $i:T''\to T'$ obtained in Step 1. Pullback gives an equivalence of small etale topoi. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $T'_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every $n\geq0$, its cohomology clause gives $H^n(T'_{\mathrm{et}},F)\cong H^n(T''_{\mathrm{et}},i^{-1}F)$, which is the claimed identification.
